choices.text: A hand that beats bluffs and loses to value.
A draw that is still live on the river

questions.explanation: The river is the last card. Draws that missed are air. Bluff-catchers are made hands in the middle.

questions.prompt: Live players under-bluff big river bets. The adjustment is…

choices.text: Fold more bluff-catchers than a solver chart says, especially against tight players.

questions.explanation: If they rarely bluff, a bluff-catcher is a fold. You do not need to hero-call to be balanced.

questions.prompt: Raising the river as a bluff is…

choices.text: Rare. Most live river raises should be value.

questions.explanation: A raise folds out bluffs and gets called by better. Value raises are the nuts.

questions.prompt: You beat their betting range. The action is…

choices.text: Call or raise for value, depending how often they continue worse.

questions.explanation: If you are ahead of the bet, you do not fold. Raising is for when worse hands still continue.
